stem:
Meena finds two steel bars in her school laboratory drawer. One bar is a magnet and the other is a plain iron bar, but they look exactly the same.
She brings one end of bar X near the North pole of bar Y and they attract each other.
Which further test would tell Meena for certain that bar Y is a magnet?

options.text: Check whether bar Y attracts a plain iron nail.
Check whether the South pole of bar Y also attracts bar X.
Check whether one end of bar X repels one end of bar Y.
Check whether bar Y is heavier than bar X.

teacher.key_rationale: Attraction alone cannot distinguish a magnet from a plain iron bar, since a magnet attracts an unmagnetised iron bar at either pole; only repulsion, which occurs between like poles of two magnets, proves that bar Y is itself a magnet. Options A and B test attraction only, and D is irrelevant.
